what_its_for: Gatifloxacin is an antibiotic eye drop used to treat bacterial infections of the eye, such as bacterial conjunctivitis (pink eye). It works by killing the bacteria causing the infection.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before using the eye drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and gently squeeze one drop into the eye. Close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes without blinking or squinting. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: For adults and children 1 year and older: On Days 1 and 2, place 1 drop in the affected eye(s) every 2 hours while you are awake, up to 8 times per day. On Days 3 through 7, place 1 drop in the affected eye(s) up to 4 times per day while you are awake. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions, as your dose may differ.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the eye drop as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one. Try to use the drops at evenly spaced times throughout the day.
storage: Store gatifloxacin eye drops at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the eye drops. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Discard the bottle after you have completed your course of treatment or as directed by your pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye, eyelid, or any surface to keep the drops sterile. Do not wear contact lenses while you have signs of an eye infection. Avoid driving or operating machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry. Do not share this medication with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms. Avoid rubbing your infected eye(s) to prevent spreading the infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: worsening eye pain, redness, swelling, or discharge; vision changes or loss; severe eye irritation or burning that does not go away; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if your symptoms do not start to improve within a few days of starting treatment.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement in their eye infection symptoms within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. It is very important to finish the entire prescribed course of eye drops, even if your eye feels better sooner, to make sure the infection is completely cleared and to prevent it from coming back.
special_populations: Children: Gatifloxacin eye drops are approved for use in children 1 year of age and older. It is not recommended for infants under 1 year old. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. The risk to the baby from eye drops is considered very low since very little medication is absorbed into the bloodstream, but always check with your doctor first. Elderly: No special dose adjustments are typically needed for older adults using the eye drop form.
